title: Async Worker Offloading with gen_server:reply/2 & Process Hibernation
solutionExplanation: Eliminates Head-of-Line blocking by returning {noreply, State} immediately from handle_call while an offloaded worker evaluates the report and delivers the reply via gen_server:reply/2.

otpDocCards.description: Explicitly sends a reply to a client that invoked gen_server:call.
otpDocCards.complexityNote: O(1) direct message delivery to waiting client.

mentalModelCheck.question: How does returning {noreply, State} and using gen_server:reply/2 inside a spawned worker resolve Head-of-Line blocking?
mentalModelCheck.codeSnippet:
handle_call({slow_task, Data}, From, State) ->
    Self = self(),
    spawn(fun() ->
        Result = compute(Data),
        gen_server:reply(From, Result),
        Self ! task_done
    end),
    {noreply, State}.

options.label: The server returns {noreply, State} in microseconds, freeing it to serve other clients immediately while the worker computes the slow result and unblocks the original caller.
options.explanation: Correct! The server process is not blocked during computation. The From token carries the client PID and monitor tag, enabling the worker to reply directly to the client.

options.label: The client is terminated immediately and replaced with a websocket.
options.explanation: The client remains in a standard gen_server:call selective receive awaiting reply.

options.label: gen_server:reply/2 bypasses the Erlang runtime and writes directly to socket buffers.
options.explanation: gen_server:reply/2 simply sends the tagged {MRef, Reply} message to the client PID.
